NDT training in Newark: how it works for Newark employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based Level I, II and III training to employers and technicians in Newark, New Jersey, as live online theory, onsite sessions at your own facility, or a blend of both, all under ASNT Level III oversight. There is no Atlantis classroom building in Newark or elsewhere in New Jersey. Your employer's written practice defines certification, a Level III gives the exams, and the employer certifies you. Refinery contractors, terminal operators, port and bridge crews, and fabrication shops use the training for UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET.

The Newark area packs a lot of inspection demand into a few miles of the Passaic River, Newark Bay and the Arthur Kill. Within a short drive there are refinery and chemical units, bulk liquid terminals, a large container port, an international airport, power stations, and some of the most heavily travelled bridges and rail structures in the country. A technician here can spend spring on a turnaround, summer on tank-floor scanning and autumn on a bridge deck. The common thread is documentation. Owners, authorised inspectors and transportation agencies all want to know that the procedure is qualified, that the person is certified to the employer's written practice for that method and level, and that the records will hold up in an audit.

Most Newark-area enquiries come from four kinds of organisation. First, inspection and mechanical contractors who supply crews to refinery and petrochemical turnarounds in Linden, Elizabeth and the wider Arthur Kill corridor. Second, terminal and tank-farm operators in Newark, Bayonne, Carteret and Sewaren, whose storage tanks and piping run on API inspection plans. Third, steel fabricators and erectors working on bridges, transit and building structure for public owners in the New York–New Jersey region. Fourth, plant maintenance teams at power stations, pharmaceutical and chemical plants across Essex, Union, Middlesex and Hudson counties. Each needs a different method mix, so we build the course plan around your scope. Request a Newark training quote and tell us what your people inspect.

Newark, New Jersey hub and Level III consulting: where each page fits

This page covers training for Newark employers and technicians. For statewide coverage, including South Jersey's refining and nuclear corridor, see NDT training in New Jersey. If you need a Level III to write procedures, review a written practice or act as your outside Level III, see refining NDT Level III consulting in Newark and NDT consulting across New Jersey. Many Newark contractors use both: consulting to bring the written practice and procedures up to owner expectations, then training to qualify the crew against them.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Newark

Every course follows the ASNT SNT-TC-1A recommended practice. Level I and Level II courses cover principles, equipment, calibration, technique, and interpretation against an approved procedure. Level III preparation covers the Basic examination, the method examinations, and the procedure-writing and programme skills a Level III needs. SNT-TC-1A's recommended classroom hours and experience for each method and level are in our training-requirements matrix. Your written practice, or an owner's contractor-qualification rules, can ask for more.

MethodLevelsWhat Newark employers use it forPrerequisite

PAUT (phased array UT)II, III prepWeld examination in place of RT during turnarounds, corrosion mapping on tank shells and vessels, bridge weld examinationUT Level II or concurrent UT training, per written practice

In a refinery-and-terminal market the weld and thickness methods dominate, so UT, PAUT and RT usually come first. Pharmaceutical and food plants lean on PT and VT for stainless systems, and exchanger-heavy plants need ET. Tell us which owners you work for and we will recommend a method order.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Newark, step by step

SNT-TC-1A is employer-based. A training course, a college or the state does not certify you. Your employer does, under its written practice. This is the sequence a Newark technician goes through:

  1. The employer's written practice. Your employer documents how it trains, examines and certifies personnel in each method and level. If you need one, start with written-practice development.
  2. Formal training hours. Classroom or live-online instruction at the hours the written practice sets. Atlantis delivers this part. Minimums by method are in the requirements matrix.
  3. On-the-job experience. Supervised experience in the method, logged and signed, on your employer's work.
  4. General, specific and practical examinations. Given by a Level III or designated examiner under the written practice. The practical is done on real specimens with real equipment.
  5. Vision examination. Near-vision acuity and colour contrast, at least annually as the written practice requires.
  6. Certification by the employer. The employer signs, backed by the Level III's records.
  7. Recertification. At the written-practice interval, by evidence of continued satisfactory work or re-examination.

Newark contractors often move technicians between owners and between contractors. Certification does not travel automatically. A new employer has to certify you under its own written practice, though it can use your existing training and experience records as evidence. Keep copies. For more on the employer model see SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Newark crews

Newark teams train with Atlantis in one of three ways.

  • Live online theory. Instructor-led sessions with a Level III on a timetable that works around shifts and turnaround rotations. This suits individual technicians and contractors who cannot release a whole crew at once. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite at your facility. We bring the course to your shop, yard or plant, and use your instruments and representative components as specimens where the written practice allows. For crews of several people, this avoids travel and keeps the course tied to the work.
  • Blended. Theory online, then a compact onsite block for hands-on technique and practical examinations under Level III supervision.

Timing is the hard part in this market. Refinery and chemical turnarounds in the Arthur Kill corridor pull every certified technician in the region onto the job, usually in spring and autumn. The best time to train is in the weeks before, so new Level IIs are ready when the work starts. Tell us your turnaround calendar and we will plan around it. Ask about onsite training for your Newark crew. Cohort and onsite quotes come back within one business day. Contractors with several branches can also look at corporate NDT training programmes.

Where NDT technicians work in Newark

  • Refining and petrochemicals. The Bayway refinery complex in Linden and its neighbouring chemical and cogeneration units are the largest single source of fixed-equipment inspection work in north Jersey. Vessel and piping inspection follows ASME Section V for NDT technique, ASME B31.3 for process piping construction, and API 510 and API 570 inspection programmes run by authorised inspectors. NDT technicians do the examinations those inspectors rely on.
  • Bulk liquid terminals. Storage terminals in Newark, Bayonne, Carteret, Sewaren and along the Kill van Kull hold fuels, chemicals and edible oils. Tank inspection to API 653 involves UT thickness, floor scanning, MT and VT on shell and nozzle welds, and vacuum-box testing.
  • Port Newark–Elizabeth. Container cranes, wharf structures, fendering and terminal equipment need MT, UT and VT. The Port Authority of New York and New Jersey and terminal operators set the contract requirements.
  • Bridges, rail and transit. The region's steel bridges, elevated highways and rail structures, including long-running rehabilitation programmes on structures such as the Pulaski Skyway, generate steady UT, MT and VT work. New steel bridge welding is usually inspected to AWS D1.5.
  • Power generation. Gas-fired stations in Linden, Kearny, Bergen and Sewaren need boiler, HRSG, piping and condenser inspection during outages. ET and UT are central.
  • Aviation. Newark Liberty International Airport supports airline maintenance and component work, where NDT follows the aircraft manufacturer's NDT manuals and the airline's FAA-approved programme. Many aviation employers certify to NAS 410 rather than SNT-TC-1A. Atlantis does not offer NAS 410 training. We mention it only so you know what aviation employers may ask for.
  • Pharmaceutical and specialty chemical plants. Central and northern New Jersey hosts a large pharmaceutical manufacturing base. Stainless process piping, vessels and clean utilities need PT, VT and UT, often to ASME BPE.

Radiation licensing and TWIC in New Jersey

New Jersey became an NRC Agreement State on 30 September 2009. Industrial radiography with sealed sources is licensed and inspected by the New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection under N.J.A.C. 7:28, which includes a subchapter on licences and radiation-safety requirements for industrial radiography. X-ray equipment registration also falls under NJDEP's radiation protection rules. A radiography company working in New Jersey needs the right state licence or reciprocity, and its radiographers must meet the radiation-safety training and certification rules, usually including certification from a recognised independent radiographer certification programme. That is separate from your SNT-TC-1A RT certification, which covers technique and interpretation. Our RT courses teach the method and do not replace the state's radiation-safety requirements. Confirm current rules with NJDEP before mobilising.

Refinery docks, bulk terminals and Port Newark–Elizabeth are facilities regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act. Unescorted access to their secure areas requires a Transportation Worker Identification Credential (TWIC) from the TSA. Refinery owners usually add their own site safety orientation and contractor qualification. For many Newark jobs, TWIC is as much a hiring requirement as Level II certification, so apply early.

Method spotlight: PAUT and TOFD for turnaround weld examination

The method that most changes a Newark technician's job prospects is phased array UT, ideally with TOFD alongside it. Turnaround schedules are tight, and radiography clears the area around the shot, which stops other trades from working. Owners and contractors increasingly accept encoded PAUT, with TOFD for height sizing, in place of RT for many piping and vessel welds, provided the procedure is qualified and the technician is certified for it. That puts a premium on technicians who can build a scan plan that covers the weld volume, set up and verify focal laws, recognise geometric and mode-converted signals, and produce encoded data an authorised inspector can review. Our PAUT and TOFD Level II courses focus on scan planning, data quality and reporting as much as on the instrument. Before your exams, use UT Level 2 practice questions to check your basics.

Local options compared: NDT training around Newark

Many people searching for NDT training in Newark want a list of options. Here is an honest one, based on what we could confirm at the time of writing. Check details with each provider.

  • Community and technical colleges. We could not confirm a dedicated NDT degree or certificate programme at a community college in northern New Jersey. Local colleges such as Essex County College and the county colleges in Union and Middlesex counties offer welding, engineering technology and manufacturing programmes that can lead into NDT jobs. The nearest regional college NDT programme we know of is the Community College of Philadelphia's non-credit Nondestructive Testing programme, developed with the US Navy, which covers VT, PT, MT and UT. The ASNT educational directory lists programmes nationwide.
  • Private schools and commercial training companies. Several commercial NDT training providers serve the New York–New Jersey area with classroom courses. These suit individuals who want scheduled public classes.
  • Inspection companies and contractor in-house programmes. Large inspection and mechanical contractors in the region train and certify their own people. If you can get hired as a trainee, this is a common route.
  • ASNT local section. The Metro New York / Northern New Jersey Section of ASNT covers Newark. Its meetings are a practical way to meet Level IIIs, employers and other technicians.
  • Atlantis NDT. Live online theory with an ASNT Level III, onsite cohorts at your facility, written-practice support and Level III services for the employer. Atlantis suits contractors and owners who need crews trained to their own written practice, and individuals whose employer will certify them. Atlantis does not run a physical school in Newark and does not offer API, AWS CWI or NAS 410 certification.

Level III services and written practices for Newark NDT companies

Refinery owners and authorised inspectors audit contractors, and the first thing they ask for is the paperwork: the written practice, qualified procedures, examination records, vision checks and OJT logs. Many Newark contractors have competent technicians but a written practice that is out of date, does not cover PAUT or TOFD, or does not match the owner's contractor-qualification requirements.

Atlantis supports Newark employers with:

  • Written-practice development, or a gap review of your current one against SNT-TC-1A and owner requirements.
  • Method procedures, including PAUT and TOFD procedures written to ASME Section V and the referencing code.
  • Examination preparation and administration under your written practice by an ASNT Level III.
  • Audit preparation, so that records are complete before an owner or authorised inspector arrives.
  • Outside Level III services for contractors who do not employ one. See refining NDT consulting in Newark.

For the full employer model see SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Newark company.

Practise before the practical exam

Turnaround crews rarely get spare time on the equipment. The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in five environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. The storage-tank and oil-and-gas scenes match a lot of Newark work. See also Practical NDT in Newark.

The simulator is for practice. It does not replace the practical examination, which under SNT-TC-1A is performed on real specimens with real equipment and graded by a Level III.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT. He sets the course content, reviews written practices and procedures, and oversees examinations under the employer's programme. For candidates preparing for Level III, see ASNT Level III training.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Newark

How do I get NDT certified in Newark, NJ?

Under SNT-TC-1A, your employer certifies you. You complete formal training in the method, build supervised experience, pass general, specific and practical examinations under the employer's written practice, and pass a vision test. Atlantis provides the training and can support the examinations and the written practice. If you have no employer yet, a Level I course in UT, MT or PT is a reasonable first step.

Can I take NDT training online in New Jersey?

Yes, for theory. Live online classes with a Level III can cover the classroom hours your written practice requires. The practical examination must be done in person on real specimens. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

That depends on your written practice and on whether you already hold UT Level I. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum classroom hours and experience for each level, and employers can require more. Current figures are in our training-requirements matrix. Experience usually takes longer to build than classroom hours.

Do I need a licence for radiography in New Jersey?

The company needs a radioactive-material licence from NJDEP, or the right reciprocity, to perform industrial radiography with sealed sources in New Jersey. Radiographers must meet the state's radiation-safety training and certification rules, usually including certification from a recognised independent programme. That is separate from your SNT-TC-1A RT certification. Check current rules with NJDEP.

Do I need a TWIC card for refinery or port NDT work around Newark?

For unescorted access to secure areas of facilities regulated under the Maritime Transportation Security Act, yes. That covers Port Newark–Elizabeth, most bulk terminals and refinery docks. Many contractors treat TWIC as a hiring requirement.

What does NDT training cost in Newark?

We quote on request. The answer depends on method, level, group size and whether it runs online, onsite or blended. Send us those details and we return a quote within one business day. Get a Newark quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Newark employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard framework for refinery, terminal, fabrication and bridge NDT in New Jersey. Some employers also ask for other credentials, such as API 510, 570 or 653 inspector certification for inspector roles, AWS CWI for weld inspection, or NAS 410 for aviation work. Atlantis trains to SNT-TC-1A only and does not offer those.

Can I use the GI Bill or WIOA funding for NDT training with Atlantis?

GI Bill benefits only apply to programmes approved for VA education benefits, and WIOA funds generally go only to providers on New Jersey's eligible training provider list. Atlantis does not claim either approval. Check the VA's WEAMS search and the New Jersey training provider list if you need those funds. Many technicians have their employer pay for training instead, which is the usual route for SNT-TC-1A certification.

Can you train our crew before a Linden-area turnaround?

Yes. Tell us the turnaround dates, methods and headcount. We usually suggest live online theory followed by an onsite practical block at your facility, timed so certifications are in place before mobilisation.

Does Atlantis have a training centre in Newark?

No. Atlantis has no physical training centre in Newark or any other city. Training runs live online or onsite at your facility.

Which NDT methods are most in demand around Newark?

UT thickness and weld examination, PAUT and TOFD for turnaround and vessel work, RT for piping, and MT, PT and VT on welds and structures. ET matters at power stations and exchanger-heavy plants.

What do NDT technicians earn around Newark?

Pay depends on method, level, overtime and union status, and turnaround work is paid differently from shop work. For a sourced overview, see our NDT salary guide.
